description: Research results produced with AI agents and checked by machine where possible: Lean 4 proofs, certificates with checkers, reproducible empirical evaluations. Each entry states its claim, its evidence, its limits and how to rerun the checks.

status_levels.lean-proof: The claim is a Lean 4 theorem; the build checks it and prints its axioms.
status_levels.certificate: The claim follows from an explicit object in the repository and a checker that verifies it.
status_levels.reproducible-empirical: Every reported number is recomputed from stored measurements by a script; the underlying method is evaluated, not proved.
status_levels.archival-analysis: An analysis of public observational data with code and archive identifiers; conclusions are interpretive.

entries.title: Large grid sets without isosceles right triangles
entries.claim: F(n) >= c * n^alpha / sqrt(log n) with alpha = 2 log 313 / log 3757 = 1.3961707..., where F(n) is the largest subset of {0,...,n-1}^2 containing no isosceles right triangle in any orientation. Previous exponent 1.317865 (Karolyi and Solymosi, arXiv:2607.22828).

verification.statement: If 3757^m <= n^2, the n x n grid contains a set without isosceles right triangles with at least floor(313^m / (m * 2^312 + 1)) points.
verification.command: cd math/triangle-free-grids/lean && lake exe cache get && lake build

limitations: The Lean theorem has a log n factor where the paper bound has sqrt(log n).
The Lean certificate check relies on native_decide.
The constant c is astronomically small; the result concerns growth rates only.
entries.produced_by: AI agents (Claude Code; an earlier 253-digit alphabet by OpenAI Codex)

entries.title: Unicyclic graphs with three distinct distance eigenvalues
entries.claim: A finite connected unicyclic graph has exactly three distinct distance eigenvalues if and only if it is isomorphic to the cycle C4 or the cycle C5. This answers Problem 1 of Hayat, Khan and Alenazi, Axioms 13 (2024), 494.

verification.statement: MainStatement: for every finite type V and simple graph G on V that is connected with as many edges as vertices, the distance matrix has exactly three distinct real eigenvalues iff G is isomorphic to cycleGraph 4 or cycleGraph 5.
verification.command: cd math/unicyclic-distance-spectra/lean && lake exe cache get && lake build

limitations: Not peer reviewed.
The Lean proof follows a different route than the written note.
builds_on: Hayat, Khan, Alenazi, On Some Distance Spectral Characteristics of Trees, Axioms 13 (2024), 494
entries.produced_by: AI agents (OpenAI Codex for the proof and the Lean formalization; Claude Code for the frozen statement and review)

entries.title: A (56, 20, 5) covering design with 336 blocks
entries.claim: C(56, 20, 5) <= 336: 336 subsets of size 20 of a 56-point set cover every 5-subset. The Covering Repository listed 693 on 2026-11-20. Also C(56, 21, 5) <= 336 and C(55, 20, 5) <= 336. Lower bound 317 (Schoenheim).
limitations: Upper bound only; the optimum is open.
Not yet submitted to the Covering Repository.
entries.produced_by: AI agents (OpenAI Codex for the construction; Claude Code for the rebuild and checkers)

entries.title: July 2026 drainage of a western Greenland supraglacial lake
entries.claim: A known Greenland basin lost 5.377 square kilometres of exposed water area between 20 and 23 July 2026, a 92.4% decline corroborated by Landsat and Sentinel-1 radar.
limitations: Water volume, flow path and active drainage duration remain unresolved.
Historical inventories already contain the basin. The novelty search concerns the July 2026 episode.
entries.produced_by: OpenAI Codex agents, using observations by the credited survey and network teams

entries.subfield: terrestrial laser scanning; forest remote sensing
entries.title: Wind correction for tree laser scans
entries.claim: On 97 published simulated S5 scan pairs (Weiser, Tabernig and Hoefle 2026), mean 3D endpoint error of per-point displacement fell from 11.78 cm (MV-Tree-LNDP) to 8.98 cm (WindReg96 with local correction), a 23.77% reduction; 22.37% on 11 newly simulated trees.
limitations: The headline comparison is retrospective: the published test pairs were known during method development.
Simulation only; no real scans with per-point motion labels.
The fraction of points within the strict accuracy threshold decreased (30.26% to 26.90%) while mean error improved.
On two unseen willow presets the effect is not significant (95% interval -4.88% to +10.64%).
The pre-registered 189-tree cohort is not yet scored.

entries.title: An apparently uncataloged earthquake in the Brawley swarm
entries.claim: Ten stations support a small local earthquake near Brawley at about 03:30:02 UTC on 10 May 2026, with a relative magnitude estimate of 1.4 and no matching event in the six catalog products checked.
limitations: The magnitude is relative to CI41460424. The new event has no independent hypocenter or calibrated magnitude.
The six catalog products overlap. A catalog omission does not establish discovery priority.
entries.produced_by: OpenAI Codex agents, using observations by the credited survey and network teams

entries.title: Locating the 2.709-day eclipse near TIC 349414709
entries.claim: Forty TESS eclipse timings and Bochum photometry locate a published signal near TIC 349414709, about 15 arcseconds from the originally listed target TIC 349414705.
limitations: The eclipse was published by IJspeert et al. in 2024.
Two Gaia sources 0.918 arcseconds apart are unresolved in eclipse. The individual component and companion mass remain open.
entries.produced_by: OpenAI Codex agents, using observations by the credited survey and network teams

entries.title: What eclipses TIC 153838604?
entries.claim: Four TESS eclipses (sectors 5, 32, 97, 98) follow a 56.0793594-day period over 2018 to 2025 (maximum residual 3.2 minutes), resolving the period alias of the duotransit candidate CTOI 153838604.01. A grazing giant planet and a faint red dwarf both fit; they predict radial-velocity semiamplitudes of 61 m/s and 6.84 km/s.
limitations: Planet versus low-mass star is not decided; radial velocities are needed.
A doubled period (112.16 days) with alternating eclipses remains possible.
An unresolved neighbouring source is not excluded.
Priority for the ephemeris has not been established.
